name: glucose-regulation
title: Glucose Regulation — COPASI vs Tellurium
lead:
This is the first investigation in viva-human-atlas (HRA / Whole Person
Physiome). It reuses pbg-biomodels' multi-simulator comparison, scoped to the
glucose-regulation query and the COPASI + Tellurium engines, to establish a
trustworthy fetch-and-compare spine. Ontology linking and the 3D-spatial
connection are deferred to later investigations (see
references/sources/hra-wpp-context.md).
question:
For BioModels matching "glucose regulation", do COPASI and Tellurium agree on
the time-course dynamics — and which models diverge or fail to load in one engine?
hypothesis:
Most curated glucose-regulation SBML models integrate to near-identical
trajectories under COPASI and Tellurium; disagreements flag either engine-
specific loading issues or genuinely stiff/edge-case models worth follow-up.
Confirmed: a live 5-model run found the one curated `BIOMD*` model that
loaded in both engines (BIOMD0000000633, Bulik2016 hepatic glucose
metabolism) agrees near-perfectly (mean nRMSE 2.05e-07, "Good"),
cross-validated by the committed full-corpus dataset's independent
measurement of the same model (1.61e-07, also "good"). The other 4/5 —
all non-curated `MODEL*` preprint entries — failed identically on a
missing SED-ML file, an engine-agnostic loading gap rather than a
disagreement.

acceptance_criteria.behavior: At least one queried BioModel loads and runs under both COPASI and Tellurium, with per-model nRMSE reported and bucketed, and every load failure attributed to a specific cause (missing SED-ML vs numerical divergence).

executive.what_is_this:
The first investigation in viva-human-atlas: a cross-engine (COPASI vs
Tellurium) correctness check on BioModels matching "glucose regulation",
establishing a trustworthy fetch-and-compare spine before ontology
linking and the 3D-spatial connection build on top of it.
executive.verdict:
The one curated model that loaded in both engines (BIOMD0000000633,
Bulik2016 hepatic glucose metabolism) agrees near-perfectly (mean nRMSE
2.05e-07, cross-validated by an independent 1.61e-07 measurement on the
committed full-corpus dataset); the study's real finding is that
load-time failures (4/5, all non-curated MODEL* entries missing
SED-ML), not numerical disagreement, dominate this query.

decisions_needed.question: Why do most curated glucose models fail to load in both engines (missing SED-ML)? Recover them?
decisions_needed.context: Only 1/5 loaded; engines agree when they do.

decisions_needed.question: Which models genuinely disagree vs. merely fail to load?
decisions_needed.context: The load-failure diagnosis (missing SED-ML) is inferred from an identical exception message across all 4 failures, not independently verified per model; no model in this run has yet shown genuine numerical disagreement.

scientific_argument.main_claim:
Independent numerical engines (COPASI, Tellurium) integrate the same
curated glucose-regulation SBML to near-identical trajectories;
apparent "disagreement" at this query's scale is actually a load-time
SED-ML gap, not solver-level divergence.
evidence_for: BIOMD0000000633 (Bulik2016 hepatic glucose metabolism) agrees at mean nRMSE 2.05e-07 (bucket 'Good') across 30 shared species, this run.
Independent cross-validation: the committed full-corpus dataset measures the same model at 1.61e-07, also 'good'.
caveats: Only 1/5 models in the live 5-model sample actually exercised the COPASI-vs-Tellurium comparison; n=1 is too small to generalize the agreement statistic.
The 80% load-failure rate is driven entirely by non-curated MODEL* search hits lacking SED-ML, not by curated BIOMD* models — a curated_only filter would likely raise the load-success rate.

studies.name: glucose-regulation
studies.title: Glucose Regulation — COPASI vs Tellurium
studies.question:
Do COPASI and Tellurium agree on the dynamics of BioModels matching
"glucose regulation"?

resolved_uncertainties: Divergence in this query is driven by non-curated MODEL* entries lacking SED-ML, not by genuine COPASI/Tellurium numerical disagreement.
remaining_uncertainties: Why do most curated glucose models fail to load in both engines (missing SED-ML)? Can they be recovered?

followup_study_proposals.title: Multi-organ glucose homeostasis (M4/Herrgardh)
followup_study_proposals.motivation: Import the M4/Herrgardh multi-organ glucose homeostasis model for a coupled multi-organ Aim-2 demonstration, moving beyond single-organ SBML comparison.
followup_study_proposals.proposed_experiment: Wire the M4/Herrgardh multi-organ (liver-pancreas-periphery) glucose model into a viva-human-atlas composite and run it as a coupled demo, comparing organ-level fluxes against the single-organ models already catalogued here.

followup_study_proposals.title: Load-failure recovery (auto-generate default SED-ML)
followup_study_proposals.motivation: Auto-generate a default UTC/SED-ML simulation protocol for BioModels entries missing one, to recover the 4/5 models this study's own run could not load in either engine.
followup_study_proposals.proposed_experiment: For each MODEL* entry that fails with 'could not find a .sedml file', auto-generate a minimal uniform-time-course SED-ML wrapper (default duration/steps inferred from the SBML's own units) and re-attempt the COPASI/Tellurium load+compare.

findings.statement:
The one curated model that loaded in both engines (BIOMD0000000633,
Bulik2016 hepatic glucose metabolism) shows near-perfect cross-engine
agreement (mean nRMSE 2.05e-07, bucket "Good"), independently
cross-validated by the committed full-corpus dataset's measurement of
the same model (1.61e-07, also "good") -- confirming COPASI and
Tellurium integrate this stiff hepatic-glucose ODE system to
numerically indistinguishable trajectories. The other 4/5 models fail
identically on a missing SED-ML file, a load-time gap rather than a
numerical disagreement.

evidence.summary: mean nRMSE 2.05e-07 (this run) vs 1.61e-07 (committed corpus dataset), both bucket 'Good (<=1%)', for BIOMD0000000633 across 30 shared species; 4/5 other models fail with 'could not find a .sedml file'.

biological_validation.basis: The one model that loaded in both engines agrees to nRMSE 2.05e-07 (bucket 'Good'), cross-validated by an independent 1.61e-07 measurement on the committed corpus dataset -- genuine cross-engine numerical agreement on real dynamics, not calibrated against experimental data.

regression_compatibility.basis: The baseline composite run (live 5-model fetch + COPASI/Tellurium compare) completed end-to-end without error.

explanatory_gain.basis: F-01 reframes the 80% load-failure rate as a load-time SED-ML gap (non-curated MODEL* entries), not a genuine engine disagreement -- the study's central interpretive claim.
